questions.history: Release the commit gate after the upstream has emitted and commit has been subscribed.
questions.prediction: The PR attributes a cancellation to the parent shortcut. On the landing the work should receive no cancellation and the subscriber should obtain 7 and normal completion after one commit, with zero rollbacks.
questions.basis: The landed regression observes cancellation directly. Normal completion of a one-element transaction supplies both its value and a reason to commit.
questions.refutation: Cancellation reaches the work on the landing, the value disappears, or completion is observed before the gated commit finishes.

questions.history: Use `Mono.error(marker)` as the work, with a manager whose rollback completes normally.
questions.prediction: Both should emit the application error, no success value, and roll back once without committing.
questions.basis: The upstream rollback test exercises an application exception. No value is available for `next()` to select on the parent.
questions.refutation: The marker is lost, commit is subscribed, or rollback is skipped.

questions.history: Using a transactional database, insert a unique id through a Mono returning the update count. After the transactional Mono completes, read that id using a separate connection to the same database.
questions.prediction: At the landing completion should imply exactly one visible row and count 1, even if commit was delayed. The parent may expose the count before the row is visible.
questions.basis: A read-committed independent connection cannot see an uncommitted insert. Issue #23304 describes that visibility gap on the related `execute(...).next()` path.
questions.refutation: The Mono completes successfully but the immediately subsequent independent read cannot find the row.
